quizzes.title: Polity and Schemes: MCQ Practice
quizzes.passage: Polity and governance decisions often turn on precise legal definitions. The Scheduled Caste list is set through an order issued in 1950, and recent court rulings have examined how a person's religion affects membership of that list. Membership is not the only area where Parliament is active. It has passed legislation that deals with the legal position of a state capital, after an arrangement in which two states shared a common capital came to an end. The government has also extended and expanded several welfare schemes. The PM Internship Scheme offers internships to young people and is run by a central ministry, while PMGSY-III is a road programme for rural habitations that has been extended for a further period. Under the Namo Drone Didi Yojana, drones are provided to rural women for agricultural work such as crop spraying and fertiliser application. Karnataka has been named a top performer under this scheme. Each scheme has a defined objective, such as connecting rural areas with the mainstream economy or empowering women in farming. Many of these programmes depend on state-level agencies to carry out the work on the ground, and their funding is shared between the Centre and the states in fixed proportions.

questions.q: The Constitution (Scheduled Castes) Order, 1950 is issued under which Article of the Constitution?
questions.explanation: The booklet states that the 1950 SC Order is issued under Article 341(1).

questions.q: Under the Doctrine of Eclipse, what happens to Scheduled Caste status when a member converts to another religion?
options: It is transferred to the Scheduled Tribe list
It is suspended, not permanently extinguished
It is restored automatically at the time of conversion
questions.explanation: The booklet says SC status is eclipsed, meaning suspended rather than permanently extinguished, and can be restored on re-conversion.

questions.q: Under the 2026 amendment, which Act's Section 5(2) was changed to name Amaravati as the capital?
questions.explanation: The amendment replaced the placeholder in Section 5(2) of the Andhra Pradesh Reorganisation Act, 2014.

questions.q:
Assertion (A): A Scheduled Caste member who converts to Christianity loses eligibility for SC status.
Reason (R): The Constitution (Scheduled Castes) Order, 1950 restricts SC membership to persons professing Hinduism, Sikhism or Buddhism.
options: Both A and R are true and R is the correct explanation of A
Both A and R are true but R is not the correct explanation of A
A is true but R is false
A is false but R is true
questions.explanation: Both statements are true, and the religion-based restriction in the 1950 Order is the reason conversion to Christianity leads to loss of SC status.

questions.q:
Match List I with List II:
I. PMGSY-III
II. Namo Drone Didi Yojana
III. PM Internship Scheme
IV. Constitution (Scheduled Castes) Order, 1950
A. Ministry of Corporate Affairs
B. Article 341(1)
C. Ministry of Rural Development
D. Department of Agriculture and Farmers Welfare
questions.explanation: PMGSY-III is nodal under the Ministry of Rural Development, the drone scheme under the Department of Agriculture and Farmers Welfare, the internship scheme under the Ministry of Corporate Affairs, and the 1950 Order under Article 341(1).

questions.q:
Examine the following statements on Scheduled Caste status:
I. Only Parliament can amend the Scheduled Caste list.
II. Scheduled Tribe status carries a religion-based bar similar to Scheduled Caste status.
III. Under the Doctrine of Eclipse, SC status is permanently extinguished on conversion.
Which of the above statements is/are correct?
questions.explanation: Only Parliament can amend the SC list, while the booklet says ST status has no religion-based bar and the Doctrine of Eclipse suspends rather than extinguishes SC status.

questions.q:
How many of the following statements are correct?
I. The Andhra Pradesh amendment names Amaravati as the sole capital.
II. The PM Internship Scheme's upper age limit is 21 years.
III. PMGSY-III has been extended till March 2028.
questions.explanation: Statements I and III match the booklet, while the upper age limit of the PM Internship Scheme is 25 years, so only two statements are correct.

quizzes.title: Schemes and Rural Roads: Typed Answer Practice
quizzes.passage: The Pradhan Mantri Gram Sadak Yojana is a centrally sponsored scheme whose objective is to provide all-weather road connectivity to rural habitations. Its third phase has been extended by the Union Cabinet for a further period, and funding is shared between the Centre and the states in fixed proportions, with the North-Eastern and Himalayan states receiving a higher central share. Implementation takes place through state-level agencies, supported by a central agency. The Namo Drone Didi Yojana aims to empower rural women by providing agricultural drones for crop spraying and precision farming. Drones are distributed to self-help groups, and the cost is met partly through a subsidy and partly through loans. The nodal authority for the drone scheme is the Department of Agriculture and Farmers Welfare. The remaining share of the cost comes through loans under the Agriculture Infrastructure Fund, and Karnataka has been named a top performer under the drone scheme. The PM Internship Scheme is open to candidates within a set age range, and it offers placements at large companies. It has been expanded to include final-year students. Insurance cover under two national life and accident schemes is also part of the internship package. Eligibility rules, including family income and government employment, decide who can apply.

questions.q: In which year was the Pradhan Mantri Gram Sadak Yojana launched?
questions.explanation: The booklet gives the launch year of PMGSY as 2000.

questions.q: Till which year has PMGSY-III been extended? (give the year)
questions.explanation: The Union Cabinet extended PMGSY-III till March 2028.

questions.q: What is the target number of drones for SHGs under the Namo Drone Didi Yojana? (number)
questions.explanation: The booklet sets the drone distribution target at 15,000 drones for SHGs.

questions.q: What is the upper age limit (in years) for the PM Internship Scheme?
questions.explanation: The age criteria under the PM Internship Scheme are 18 to 25 years.

questions.q: What is the full name of the central agency that implements PMGSY?
questions.explanation: The booklet names the National Rural Infrastructure Development Agency as PMGSY's central agency.

questions.q: The 2026 amendment amends the Andhra Pradesh Reorganisation Act of which year? (year)
questions.explanation: The amendment changes Section 5(2) of the Andhra Pradesh Reorganisation Act, 2014.

questions.q: In which year was the Prevention of Atrocities Act enacted? (year)
questions.explanation: The Scheduled Castes and Scheduled Tribes (Prevention of Atrocities) Act was enacted in 1989.

quizzes.title: Economy and Climate: MCQ Practice
quizzes.passage: India's position in global economic rankings is measured using nominal GDP in US dollar terms. The figure depends on domestic output in rupees and on the exchange rate against the dollar, so a weaker rupee lowers the dollar value of GDP. A revision of GDP data with a new base year also changes the figures. Special Additional Excise Duty, or SAED, is a levy on petroleum products that the government adjusts when global crude prices move. It works as a windfall tax in times of price surges, and unlike the GST, its revenue is kept by the Centre. Climate policy is another area of activity. Countries submit self-defined climate action plans under the Paris framework, and these plans are reported regularly. Synthetic gases used in cooling and foam industries are being phased down under an international amendment to the Montreal Protocol. Air conditioners and refrigerators are among the uses of these synthetic gases. Host nations for the UN climate conference are chosen through regional rotation. The rules also require a formal proposal to the UNFCCC Secretariat before a country can be chosen. If no host emerges, the venue shifts to Bonn, the seat of the UNFCCC. Rankings also influence investor sentiment and global confidence.

questions.q: India slipped behind which two economies in the IMF's World Economic Outlook 2026 nominal GDP ranking?
questions.explanation: The booklet states that India slipped from 4th to 6th place, behind the United Kingdom and Japan.

questions.q: Under which section of the Finance Act, 2002 is Special Additional Excise Duty levied?
questions.explanation: The booklet gives the legal basis of SAED as Section 147 of the Finance Act, 2002.

questions.q: Which company leads the first semiconductor fabrication SEZ at Dholera in Gujarat?
questions.explanation: The booklet names Tata Semiconductor as leading the Dholera SEZ in partnership with Taiwan's PSMC.

questions.q:
Assertion (A): India has withdrawn its bid to host COP33 in 2028.
Reason (R): India has hosted the UN climate conference (COP8) only once, in New Delhi in 2002.
options: Both A and R are true and R is the correct explanation of A
Both A and R are true but R is not the correct explanation of A
A is true but R is false
A is false but R is true
questions.explanation: Both statements are true, but India having hosted COP8 in 2002 does not explain why it withdrew its COP33 bid.

questions.q:
Match List I with List II:
I. NDC 3.0 emission intensity reduction
II. NDC 3.0 non-fossil capacity share
III. NDC 2.0 emission intensity reduction
IV. NDC 2.0 non-fossil capacity share
A. 47 per cent
B. 60 per cent
C. 45 per cent
D. 50 per cent
questions.explanation: NDC 3.0 targets a 47 per cent emission intensity cut and 60 per cent non-fossil capacity, while NDC 2.0 targets 45 and 50 per cent respectively.

questions.q:
Examine the following statements on climate and synthetic gases:
I. HFCs were introduced as replacements for ozone-depleting substances such as CFCs.
II. Nationally Determined Contributions are legally binding targets under the Paris framework.
III. The Kigali Amendment is legally binding and recognises differentiated responsibilities.
Which of the above statements is/are correct?
questions.explanation: Statements I and III match the booklet, while NDCs are described as not legally binding targets but subject to mandatory reporting.

questions.q:
How many of the following statements are correct?
I. India has slipped to sixth place in nominal GDP in the IMF's World Economic Outlook 2026.
II. India ratified the Kigali Amendment in 2021.
III. The Kigali Amendment was adopted under the Kyoto Protocol.
questions.explanation: Statements I and II are correct, while the Kigali Amendment was adopted under the Montreal Protocol, so only two statements are correct.

quizzes.title: Economy and Climate: Typed Answer Practice
quizzes.passage: Economic rankings depend on how an economy's output is valued. Countries are compared by nominal GDP in dollar terms, so the figures move with the exchange rate. When the domestic currency weakens, the same output is worth fewer dollars. The government also revises GDP series when a new base year is introduced, and such revisions change the level of output reported for earlier years. Separately, the government uses a special duty on petroleum products that is revised regularly, and its revenue is not divided with states the way GST revenue is. States therefore receive no share of that revenue, which goes to the Central Government. On the climate side, countries prepare national climate plans under the Paris framework, which are reported and updated over time. Such plans are not legally binding, but reporting is mandatory. The host of the annual UN climate conference is chosen through a rotation among regional groups. Finally, the use of synthetic gases in cooling and foam is being restricted under an international agreement aimed at reducing global warming. The ranking figures are therefore sensitive to currency movements and to statistical revisions. A fall in rank does not by itself signal an economic slowdown. India remains among the fastest-growing major economies.

questions.q: By what percentage (per cent) does NDC 3.0 aim to cut emission intensity from 2005 levels?
questions.explanation: The booklet gives a 47 per cent reduction in emission intensity from 2005 levels under NDC 3.0.

questions.q: In which year was the Kigali Amendment adopted?
questions.explanation: The booklet says the Kigali Amendment was adopted in 2016 in Rwanda.

questions.q: In which year did India ratify the Kigali Amendment?
questions.explanation: The booklet states that India ratified the Kigali Amendment in 2021.

questions.q: In which city did India host COP8 in 2002?
questions.explanation: The booklet says India has hosted COP8 once, in New Delhi, in 2002.

questions.q: In which year was the Central Excise Act, to which SAED is linked, enacted? (year)
questions.explanation: The booklet says SAED is linked to the Central Excise Act, 1944.

questions.q: Which company leads the first semiconductor fabrication SEZ at Dholera? (name)
questions.explanation: The booklet names Tata Semiconductor as leading the Dholera fabrication SEZ with Taiwan's PSMC.

questions.q: Under the Kigali Amendment, from which year is HFC consumption to be frozen for India? (year)
questions.explanation: The booklet lists 2028 as the year to freeze HFC consumption under the Kigali Amendment.

quizzes.title: Historical Events and Personalities: MCQ Practice
quizzes.passage: Several episodes in the history of India show how political events shaped public life. A battle near Panipat, in present-day Haryana, is remembered as a turning point in medieval history, and its military methods drew on techniques from West Asia. The Sikh community was shaped by a line of Gurus who built towns and developed their own institutions. Their teachings and practices were preserved and passed on over generations. In 1919, a gathering in Amritsar on a spring festival day was fired on by colonial troops, and the incident caused deep anger across the country. Protests that followed were linked to laws that allowed detention without trial, and to the arrest of local leaders. An official inquiry criticised the commander but imposed no severe punishment. The gathering had come together for a Baisakhi celebration and to protest against recent arrests. The massacre is still remembered as one of the most brutal episodes of colonial rule. Reformers of the nineteenth and twentieth centuries also worked for social change. One campaigned for the education of women and the rights of lower castes, and another helped draft the Constitution of India. The Non-Cooperation Movement of 1920, led by Gandhi, marked a shift in the freedom struggle. Their work is commemorated through national observances.

questions.q: Which military strategy, used in the battle near Panipat, involved dividing the army into flanking units that attacked from the sides and rear?
questions.explanation: The booklet describes the Tulughma strategy as dividing the army into flanking units attacking from the sides and rear.

questions.q: Who translated Babur's Turkish autobiography into Persian as the Baburnama?
questions.explanation: The booklet credits Abdur Rahim Khan-i-Khana with the Persian translation of Babur's autobiography.

questions.q: What official death toll is cited for the Jallianwala Bagh Massacre?
questions.explanation: The booklet gives the official death toll as 379, while the INC estimate is over 1000.

questions.q:
Assertion (A): Guru Tegh Bahadur was executed in Delhi on the orders of Aurangzeb.
Reason (R): He was executed for defending the freedom of religion.
options: A is true but R is false
A is false but R is true
Both A and R are true and R is the correct explanation of A
Both A and R are true but R is not the correct explanation of A
questions.explanation: Both statements are true, and the booklet links his execution to his defence of freedom of religion.

questions.q:
Match List I with List II:
I. Battle of Khanwa (1527)
II. Battle of Chanderi (1528)
III. First Battle of Panipat (1526)
IV. Jallianwala Bagh Massacre (1919)
A. Ibrahim Lodi
B. Medini Rai
C. Rana Sanga
D. Reginald Dyer
questions.explanation: Khanwa was fought against Rana Sanga, Chanderi against Medini Rai, Panipat against Ibrahim Lodi, and Reginald Dyer was the perpetrator at Jallianwala Bagh.

questions.q:
Examine the following statements about the Sikh Gurus:
I. Guru Nanak Dev started the Guru ka Langar.
II. Guru Tegh Bahadur founded the Khalsa in 1699.
III. Guru Arjun Dev composed the Adi Granth in 1604.
Which of the above statements is/are correct?
questions.explanation: Statements I and III match the booklet, while the Khalsa was founded in 1699 by Guru Gobind Singh, not Guru Tegh Bahadur.

questions.q:
How many of the following statements are correct?
I. The First Battle of Panipat marked the foundation of the Mughal Empire in India.
II. Shaheed Diwas is observed on 23 March.
III. Dr B. R. Ambedkar received the Bharat Ratna in 1956.
questions.explanation: Statements I and II are correct, while Ambedkar received the posthumous Bharat Ratna in 1990, so only two statements are correct.

quizzes.title: Sikh History and Reformers: Typed Answer Practice
quizzes.passage: Historical episodes in India are often remembered through anniversaries and observances. Sikh history is shaped by a line of Gurus whose teachings and institutions developed the community over more than two centuries. The first of them is regarded as the founder of the faith, while later Gurus built towns, established shared meals for visitors and oversaw the creation of sacred texts. A military campaign in the early sixteenth century is also part of this history. The invader who fought near Panipat had earlier held territory in Central Asia, and the battle is remembered as a turning point in medieval India. The battle is also linked to the later Mughal empire in India, and Panipat is in present-day Haryana. Reformers of the nineteenth and twentieth centuries also left a lasting mark. One opened a school for girls in Pune with his wife, while another campaigned against caste discrimination and later helped draft the Constitution. A young revolutionary generation is remembered too, including men who were executed in a Lahore jail in the 1930s and are honoured every year. Such figures are honoured on national days, with tributes from national leaders. The events and figures in this section show how faith, war and social reform shaped modern India.

questions.q: At what age (in years) did Babur seize Kabul in 1504?
questions.explanation: The booklet states that Babur seized Kabul at the age of 24 in 1504.

questions.q: In which year did Guru Gobind Singh found the Khalsa? (year)
questions.explanation: The booklet says Guru Gobind Singh founded the Khalsa in 1699.

questions.q: In which year did Guru Arjun Dev compose the Adi Granth? (year)
questions.explanation: The booklet states that Guru Arjun Dev composed the Adi Granth in 1604.

questions.q: In which year was the first indigenous girls' school in Pune, set up by the Phules, established? (year)
questions.explanation: The booklet says Jyotirao and Savitribai Phule established the girls' school in Pune in 1848.

questions.q: In which year did Dr B. R. Ambedkar convert to Buddhism? (year)
questions.explanation: The booklet states that Ambedkar converted to Buddhism in 1956.

questions.q: On which date is Shaheed Diwas observed? (day and month)
questions.explanation: The booklet says Shaheed Diwas is observed on 23 March, marking the 1931 execution of Bhagat Singh, Sukhdev and Rajguru.

questions.q: Which Sikh Guru founded Anandpur Sahib? (name)
questions.explanation: The booklet says Guru Tegh Bahadur, the 9th Sikh Guru, founded Anandpur Sahib.
